Design & EDA7 firms · 3 critical

Design & EDA

  1. Cadence Design Systems

    United States, San Jose · CDNS

    Chokepoint level: Critical

    Digital and analog implementation, verification, IP

    The second-largest of the three main makers of chip design (EDA) software, strong in analog and custom design, simulation and hardware emulation. Designers verify large AI chips on its Palladium and Protium emulation systems, which run a design in hardware before it goes to the fab.

    Customers
    Nvidia, Broadcom, Marvell, MediaTek, Samsung, Micron
    Share
    About $5.30B of calendar 2025 EDA revenue, second behind Synopsys
    Founded
    1988
    Ownership
    Public
    Revenue
    $5,296,759 thousand (2025)
    From China
    12.8% of revenue, FY2025

    Source

  2. Siemens EDA

    United States, Wilsonville

    Chokepoint level: Critical

    Design for test, physical verification, Calibre

    The third-largest maker of chip design (EDA) software. Its Calibre tool is the de facto standard for physical verification, the check foundries use to confirm a layout follows their manufacturing rules before they accept it. It also sells design-for-test software. Foundries write the rule files they give chip designers in Calibre's format.

    Customers
    TSMC, Samsung, Intel, GlobalFoundries, Nvidia
    Share
    Estimated $2.2-2.5B of calendar 2025 EDA revenue, third behind Synopsys and Cadence. The EDA country share counts it under Germany, its parent's home
    Founded
    1981
    Ownership
    Subsidiary of Siemens AG of Germany (acquired as Mentor Graphics in 2017)

    Source

  3. Synopsys

    United States, Sunnyvale · SNPS

    Chokepoint level: Critical

    Full-flow EDA, silicon IP and simulation

    Makes the synthesis, place-and-route, verification and signoff software that turns the code describing an AI accelerator's logic (its RTL) into a layout a fab can build. It also sells the largest commercial catalog of silicon IP, ready-made circuit blocks that chip designers license. Its 2025 acquisition of Ansys added multiphysics simulation for thermal and power integrity.

    Customers
    Nvidia, AMD, Apple, TSMC, Samsung, Intel
    Share
    About $8B of calendar 2025 EDA and IP revenue including Ansys, against Cadence at $5.30B and Siemens EDA at an estimated $2.2-2.5B
    Founded
    1986
    Ownership
    Public
    Revenue
    $7,054,178 thousand (year to October 2025)
    From China
    11.5% of revenue, year to Oct 2025

    Source

  4. Ansys

    United States, Canonsburg

    Chokepoint level: Important

    Multiphysics, thermal and power integrity simulation

    Makes the thermal, electromagnetic and structural simulation software used to model how a 1 kW accelerator package heats, warps and delivers power. Its RedHawk tool is the standard for power integrity signoff, the final check that power reaches every part of a chip as designed.

    Customers
    Nvidia, AMD, TSMC, Samsung, Intel
    Founded
    1970
    Ownership
    Subsidiary of Synopsys since the acquisition closed in 2025

    About the revenue figure. Ansys has filed no accounts since Synopsys bought it in July 2025, so this is its last annual figure.

IP & Architecture5 firms · 1 critical

IP & Architecture

  1. Arm Holdings

    United Kingdom, Cambridge · ARM

    Chokepoint level: Critical

    CPU instruction set and core IP

    Licenses the CPU architecture and cores used in the host processors that feed data to AI accelerators. These include Nvidia's Grace and Vera CPUs and the Arm cores inside the server chips that large cloud companies design. It also licenses the interconnect and system IP around them. In 2026 it launched the Arm AGI CPU, its first production chip. By May 2026, ASRock, Lenovo, Quanta and Supermicro were taking orders for servers built on it.

    Customers
    Nvidia, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, MediaTek, Qualcomm
    Founded
    1990
    Ownership
    Public, majority owned by SoftBank Group
    Revenue
    $4,920 million (year to March 2026)

    Chokepoint level: Important

    The third-largest wafer maker, with fabs in Taiwan, Japan, the US and Europe. It built a new 300 mm plant in Sherman, Texas, with CHIPS Act support.   3. Shin-Etsu Chemical信越化学工業

    Japan, Tokyo · 4063.T

    Chokepoint level: Important

    300 mm polished and epitaxial wafers, photoresist, pellicles

    The world's largest silicon wafer maker by capacity and shipments. Silicon wafers are the blank discs every logic and memory die is built on. Shin-Etsu held an estimated 22 percent of global 300 mm wafer capacity at the end of 2024, according to the October 2025 listing prospectus of the Chinese wafer maker Eswin. It also makes ArF and EUV photoresist, the light-sensitive coating chip patterns are printed into, and pellicles, the thin films that keep dust off photomasks. So it supplies three separate stages of the chain.
